findings.reason: All three authentic original standalone screenshot tiles show the full theorem and proof without a figure. A diagram is warranted to distinguish projection to the oriented core from inclusion into the exterior: they kill different preferred-basis generators. The fork of homology maps makes the central longitude characterization concrete without suggesting that an arbitrary product section is already preferred.

correction: Appended an explanatory peripheral homology diagram with p_*:(a,b) -> bc and i_*:(a,b) -> ag; explicitly distinguished the original product section sigma from lambda=sigma-k mu. No existing text or frontmatter was changed.

diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement and F8 identify H_1(T_K;Z) with Z^2. Proof steps 5.1–6.1 give H_1(E_K;Z)=Z g for g=i_*[mu]. F6 gives H_1(S^1;Z)=Z c. Both drawn arrows start at H_1(T_K;Z); p_* targets H_1(S^1;Z), and i_* targets H_1(E_K;Z), exactly as induced by the maps in the Statement.

The positive fibre meridian has constant product projection and hence p_*[mu]=0. The longitude in Statement and step 7.1 has degree +1, hence p_*[lambda]=c for the positive generator c. Additivity gives p_*(a[mu]+b[lambda])=bc; no sign reversal is introduced.

Step 6.1 proves g=i_*[mu] generates the exterior homology. Step 7.1 proves i_*[lambda]=0 and that ([mu],[lambda]) is a basis, so i_*(a[mu]+b[lambda])=ag. The text explicitly retains lambda=sigma-k mu and i_*[sigma]=kg from step 7.1 rather than equating sigma and lambda.

The diagram asserts only the two induced homomorphisms and their coordinate formulas; there is no arrow or commutativity relation between the two target groups. It displays no Mayer–Vietoris boundary sign convention. The complete rigorous proof is unchanged and independent of the figure.
